title: Renewing the Mind
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Renewing the mind is the work of God by which a believer’s thinking is reshaped by Scripture, truth, and the Holy Spirit. Instead of being conformed to the world, the Christian learns to think according to God’s Word.
summary: Renewing the mind is the work of God by which a believer’s thinking is reshaped by Scripture, truth, and the Holy Spirit. Instead of being conformed to the world, the Christian learns to think according to God’s Word.
christFocus: Jesus Christ transforms His people from the inside out. Through His Word and Spirit, believers learn to set their minds on what is true, holy, eternal, and pleasing to Him.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The mind matters in discipleship. What people believe, dwell on, imagine, fear, and desire shapes the way they live. Scripture calls believers not to be conformed to this world, but to be transformed by the renewing of the mind.

Renewal means old patterns of thought must be confronted. Lies, shame, lust, bitterness, fear, pride, worldly values, and false doctrine must be brought under the truth of God’s Word.

The renewed mind is not merely more religious; it is increasingly shaped by Christ. Believers learn to think on what is true, honorable, just, pure, lovely, commendable, excellent, and praiseworthy.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many battles in the Christian life begin in the mind. A person can be physically present in church while still being ruled by old lies, anxious thoughts, worldly patterns, or sinful imagination.

This doctrine gives hope for transformation. God does not only command outward change; He renews the inner life through His truth.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Pay attention to what is shaping your thoughts. Fill your mind with Scripture, reject lies, confess sinful thought patterns, and bring anxious or tempting thoughts to Christ. Practice thinking on truth until God’s Word begins to reshape your desires, responses, and decisions.
